news.headline: Rajasthan: 80 tehsils across 14 districts declared drought-hit
news.story_lead: Rajasthan: 80 tehsils across 14 districts declared drought-hit The districts covered are Banswara, Barmer, Balotra, Bikaner, Churu, Dungarpur, Beawar, Jaisalmer, Jalore, Jodhpur, Phalodi, Nagaur, Pali and Sirohi As many as 80 tehsils across fourteen districts in Rajasthan have been declared drought-affected following deficient rainfall, reduced water availability and damage to the kharif crop. Two notifications issued by the disaster management, relief and civil defence department on October 24 and 25 classify 69 tehsils as severely drought-affected and 11 as moderately affected. The declarations will remain effective for six months from publication.
news.full_article_text: Rajasthan: 80 tehsils across 14 districts declared drought-hit The districts covered are Banswara, Barmer, Balotra, Bikaner, Churu, Dungarpur, Beawar, Jaisalmer, Jalore, Jodhpur, Phalodi, Nagaur, Pali and Sirohi As many as 80 tehsils across fourteen districts in Rajasthan have been declared drought-affected following deficient rainfall, reduced water availability and damage to the kharif crop. Two notifications issued by the disaster management, relief and civil defence department on October 24 and 25 classify 69 tehsils as severely drought-affected and 11 as moderately affected. The declarations will remain effective for six months from publication. The first notification covered 53 tehsils across 13 districts. The second added 27 tehsils across 10 districts, including Bikaner, taking the combined number of affected districts to 14. Of the additional tehsils, 25 have been classified as severely affected and two as moderately affected. The districts covered are Banswara, Barmer, Balotra, Bikaner, Churu, Dungarpur, Beawar, Jaisalmer, Jalore, Jodhpur, Phalodi, Nagaur, Pali and Sirohi. According to the notifications, the assessment considered deficient rainfall, reduced surface and groundwater availability, poor crop conditions and information from the Centre’s Drought Monitoring Portal. The assessment followed the Centre’s Drought Management Manual, 2016. Also Read: Drought-hit Latur bans use of crop residue as industrial fuel Jodhpur has the highest number of affected tehsils at 12, followed by Barmer and Jalore with 10 each, Balotra with nine, Pali with eight, and Dungarpur, Jaisalmer and Phalodi with seven each. Banswara has three, Churu and Beawar have two each, while Bikaner, Nagaur and Sirohi have one each. In Jodhpur, 11 tehsils—Osian, Tinwari, Balesar, Bawri, Shergarh, Sekhala, Kudi Bhagtasni, Jodhpur, Jhanwar, Bilara and Luni—have been classified as severely affected, while Pipar Shahar is moderately affected. All ten listed tehsils in Barmer, Gadra Road, Chohtan, Barmer, Baytoo, Sedwa, Ramsar, Sheo, Dhanau, Barmer Rural and Batadu, are severely affected. Jalore’s 10 tehsils, Ahore, Chitalwana, Jaswantpura, Bagoda, Bhinmal, Raniwara, Sanchore, Sayla, Bhadrajun and Jalore, are also in the severe category. In Balotra, Gudamalani, Kalyanpur, Pachpadra, Gida, Dhorimanna, Patodi, Samdari, Siwana and Sindhari have been classified as severely affected. All eight listed tehsils in Pali—Sumerpur, Desuri, Pali, Bali, Marwar Junction, Rani, Rohat and Sojat—are severely affected. In Jaisalmer, Fatehgarh, Mohangarh, Sam, Ramgarh, Pokaran and Phalsund are severely affected, while Jaisalmer tehsil is moderately affected. In Phalodi, Phalodi, Bap, Bapini, Aau, Ghantiyali and Dechu are in the severe category, while Setrawa is moderately affected. Dungarpur’s Aspur, Galiyakot, Jhauthri and Sabla tehsils have been classified as severely affected, while Simalwara, Paldewal and Obri are moderately affected. In Banswara, Garhi and Arthuna are severely affected and Sajjangarh is moderately affected. Rajgarh and Sidhmukh in Churu, and Sheoganj in Sirohi, have been placed in the severe category. Raipur and Jaitaran in Beawar, Khinvsar in Nagaur and Hada in Bikaner have been classified as moderately affected. Below-normal monsoon According to the Water Resources Department’s report dated September 30 , Rajasthan received 350.83 mm of rainfall between June 1 and September 30 against a normal of 424.71 mm, a shortfall of 73.88 mm. Also Read: Sule seeks ₹ 9,000 aid for farmers, demands ₹ 1L per hectare relief The department classified 14 of the state’s 41 districts as rainfall-deficient, while 24 recorded normal rainfall and three received excess rainfall. The deficient districts included Balotra, Banswara, Dungarpur, Jaisalmer, Jalore, Jodhpur, Pali and Sirohi. The same report recorded water storage in the state’s 693 monitored dams at 62.16% of their combined capacity, compared with 90.19% on the corresponding date last year. In the WRD’s Jodhpur zone, storage stood at just 15.98%, against 80.45% a year earlier.

news.story_lead: As Kharge's remark sparks row, 'heckler' clarifies 'Modi won't go anywhere' remark Mallikarjun Kharge's comment sparked a controversy, with BJP leaders accusing him of making “indecent” remarks about Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s father. The man who allegedly yelled “Modi won't go anywhere” during Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's address at an event in Bihar has clarified that what he meant was that “as long as there was no rebellion in the country, Narendra Modi won’t go anywhere.” Kharge's reaction to the man's remark was, “Modi ka baap bhi jayega” (Even Modi’s father will go). Speaking at an event to mark the 139th birth anniversary of Shrikrishna Singh, Bihar’s first chief minister, Kharge said the Congress would send those allegedly involved in irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process to jail.
news.full_article_text: As Kharge's remark sparks row, 'heckler' clarifies 'Modi won't go anywhere' remark Mallikarjun Kharge's comment sparked a controversy, with BJP leaders accusing him of making “indecent” remarks about Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s father. The man who allegedly yelled “Modi won't go anywhere” during Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's address at an event in Bihar has clarified that what he meant was that “as long as there was no rebellion in the country, Narendra Modi won’t go anywhere.” Kharge's reaction to the man's remark was, “Modi ka baap bhi jayega” (Even Modi’s father will go). Speaking at an event to mark the 139th birth anniversary of Shrikrishna Singh, Bihar’s first chief minister, Kharge said the Congress would send those allegedly involved in irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process to jail. A person in the audience responded by shouting, “Modi won’t go anywhere," drawing the retort from Kharge. Kharge's comment sparked a controversy, with BJP leaders accusing him of making “indecent” remarks about Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s father. “Kharge ji’s statement is shameful, sorrowful and utterly condemnable. But what more can one expect from a mafia gang?” the BJP said, demanding that Kharge apologise to the people of the country. Man clarifies remark Speaking to reporters later, the man who made the remark identified himself as Santhosh Kumar, a Congress worker from Chhapra. He claimed that people had mistaken him for a BJP worker because of his intervention during the event. “What I meant was that as long as there is no rebellion in the country, Narendra Modi won’t go anywhere,” he said, news agency PTI reported. BJP demands apology from Kharge What followed Kharge’s remark was criticism and a call for apology from BJP leaders . A BJP worker also filed a police complaint against him over his remarks targeting PM Modi. BJP MP Anurag Thakur said that Kharge must offer an unreserved apology to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the nation for his "indecent" remarks. Speaking to news agency ANI, he said that such statements are testaments to the “ultimate manifestation of the Congress Party’s ideological bankruptcy.” "The influence of Rahul Gandhi’s company is evident in the statements made by Mallikarjun Kharge. Such an indecent remark deserves the strongest possible condemnation. For the national president of the country’s oldest political party to make such an inappropriate comment about the father of the Prime Minister is the ultimate manifestation of the Congress Party’s ideological bankruptcy. The party has become completely devoid of ideology,” he said. “Apologise to the nation. An apology must be offered to Modi ji. The country has now seen the true face of the Congress Party and the state to which it has been reduced today," he added. Home minister Amit Shah said that Kharge has "today torn apart all norms of decorum by making an indecent remark about Modi ji's father in Patna". "This is not the first time that the Congress party has used abusive language against Modi ji or his family. At times, they have hurled insults at his revered mother, at times called him 'merchant of death,' and at times mocked his poverty by calling him 'chaiwala'. "Under Rahul Gandhi's leadership, the Congress party keeps crossing the limits of indecency every day. In the past 12 years, the repeated electoral defeats have bred such desperation and frustration in the Congress party that it no longer has any policy left, nor any issue – only the politics of slander remains," he said in a post on X. Defence minister Rajnath Singh also expressed hurt over Congress president’s remark. In a post on X, Singh said he was “stunned and hurt” by Kharge’s remark made in Patna, Bihar, regarding the Prime Minister’s father. “I am stunned and hurt by the remark made by Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge ji in Patna regarding the revered father of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. Until yesterday, Congress leaders and workers used to mock Prime Minister ji's humble family background and employ indecent language towards his esteemed mother. Today, this same level of base politics has reached the top leadership of the Congress. news.headline: Pune man gets seven years jail for feeding wife capsules containing blade pieces
news.story_lead: Pune man gets seven years jail for feeding wife capsules containing blade pieces The court also sentenced the accused husband, identified as Somnath Sadhu Sapkal, to three years of rigorous imprisonment for cruelty. A Pune sessions court has sentenced a 45-year-old man to seven years of rigorous imprisonment for attempting to murder his wife by allegedly feeding her capsules containing pieces of a blade under the pretext of giving her medicine. In the October 23 order, which was made available on Monday, the court also sentenced the accused husband, identified as Somnath Sadhu Sapkal, to three years of rigorous imprisonment for cruelty, with both sentences to run concurrently.
news.full_article_text: Pune man gets seven years jail for feeding wife capsules containing blade pieces The court also sentenced the accused husband, identified as Somnath Sadhu Sapkal, to three years of rigorous imprisonment for cruelty. A Pune sessions court has sentenced a 45-year-old man to seven years of rigorous imprisonment for attempting to murder his wife by allegedly feeding her capsules containing pieces of a blade under the pretext of giving her medicine. In the October 23 order, which was made available on Monday, the court also sentenced the accused husband, identified as Somnath Sadhu Sapkal, to three years of rigorous imprisonment for cruelty, with both sentences to run concurrently. Additional Sessions Judge Aniruddha Sulabha Subhash Gandhi convicted the accused under Sections 307 (attempt to murder) and 498A (cruelty by husband or his relatives) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). The court imposed fines of ₹ 50,000 and ₹ 20,000, respectively. The case The case arose from a complaint by Sapkal's wife, Chhaya, who alleged that her husband had been giving her capsules containing blade pieces under the pretext of administering medicine. The incidents reportedly occurred between October 2023 and November 8, 2023. Uttamnagar police registered a first information report on November 14, 2023. According to the prosecution, the woman experienced stomach pain in October 2023 and noticed a piece of a blade passing through her stool. A similar incident occurred later. On November 8, she was taken to hospital with severe abdominal pain. Doctors subsequently removed a blade piece from her stomach through an endoscopic procedure. The prosecution examined seven witnesses, including the complainant, her son, the treating doctor, a medical shop owner, panch witnesses and the investigating officer. Although the complainant and her son did not fully support the prosecution during the trial, the court relied on the medical evidence, the recovery of blade pieces and capsules from the accused's residence, and the testimony of other witnesses. The judge observed that the court had examined the seized articles during the hearing to determine whether the blade pieces could fit inside the capsules. “It was found that the pieces of the blade could be bent and placed inside the capsules. Therefore, it is clearly established that pieces of a blade could be administered to a person through capsules,” the judge observed. The court noted that a medical shop owner, Ganesh Chaudhary, had testified that Sapkal purchased a packet of Almox 500 capsules from him. The prosecution also established that the police had seized the capsule packet and two steel blade pieces from a divan at the accused's residence pursuant to his statement. Medical evidence was central to the court's findings. Dr Poonam Mantri, who treated the complainant, testified that the blade piece found in the woman's stomach posed a threat to her life. The judgement Under the final order, the accused Sapkal was sentenced to seven years of rigorous imprisonment and fined ₹ 50,000 under Section 307. He was also sentenced to three years of rigorous imprisonment and fined ₹ 20,000 under Section 498A. Both sentences will run concurrently. The court also directed that he receive the statutory set-off for the period already spent in custody. Referring to the doctor's testimony, the judge observed, “The pieces of the blade that had entered the complainant's stomach posed a danger to her life, and she could also have died as a result.” The court concluded that administering capsules containing blade pieces amounted to an attempt to murder and constituted cruelty under Section 498A of the IPC. “Feeding capsules containing pieces of a blade to the complainant amounts to an attempt to murder,” the judge held. The court further noted that the accused had allegedly given his wife the capsules over a period of approximately two months and concluded that the prosecution had established the charges under Sections 307 and 498A. However, the court found insufficient evidence to establish the separate allegations that Sapkal had assaulted and abused his wife. It acquitted him of charges under Sections 323 (voluntarily causing hurt) and 504 (intentional insult intended to provoke a breach of peace) of the IPC. During the sentencing hearing, the defence argued that Sapkal was the sole earning member of his family and that his wife was living with him and dependent on him. The court considered these submissions while deciding the punishment. The judge noted the seriousness of the offence but decided against imposing life imprisonment, opting instead for fixed terms of rigorous imprisonment.

news.headline: Death toll in Nigeria village raided by gunmen rises to 48, police say
news.story_lead: File image of Nigerian police officers - Published 25 October 2026, 03:20 GMT The death toll from Friday's attack on a remote village in the north-eastern Nigerian state of Taraba has risen to at least 48, police have told the BBC. The police had initially reported 10 deaths after unidentified gunmen on motorcycles raided the village of Binnari, looting shops and setting houses ablaze. More bodies were discovered on Sunday, according to state police spokesperson Victor Mshelizah, who said some of the victims had drowned while trying to escape the attackers while others were killed in nearby bushes.
news.full_article_text: File image of Nigerian police officers - Published 25 October 2026, 03:20 GMT The death toll from Friday's attack on a remote village in the north-eastern Nigerian state of Taraba has risen to at least 48, police have told the BBC. The police had initially reported 10 deaths after unidentified gunmen on motorcycles raided the village of Binnari, looting shops and setting houses ablaze. More bodies were discovered on Sunday, according to state police spokesperson Victor Mshelizah, who said some of the victims had drowned while trying to escape the attackers while others were killed in nearby bushes. Meanwhile, Amnesty International's director for Nigeria said his organisation had confirmed 52 deaths, citing sources on the ground and members of the local community. The attack happened just after midday Muslim prayers, and the rampage went on for up to four hours. State police had initially recovered 10 bodies with gunshot wounds after officers responded to a distress call. The attackers had fled by the time officers arrived - but they continued to patrol the area to restore calm, Taraba's police told the BBC on Saturday. "We were able to disperse the unknown gunmen though there was no casualty on their side and ours because the terrain is difficult and they're used to the terrain," Assistant Superintendent of Police Victor Mshelizah said. Community leader Malam Abubakar Saifullahi told news agency AFP that the attackers had arrived on about 50 motorcycles, two men apiece. "They looted shops and took cash, foodstuffs and other provisions," he said. "They also took motorcycles abandoned by people fleeing the attack." Isiyaku Musa, who survived the attack, told AFP: "People were running in different directions to escape the attack. Nobody knew where it was safe to go." Amnesty's Nigeria director Isa Sanusi has called for an impartial investigation into the killings, accusing the authorities of leaving rural communities "at the mercy of gunmen that are repeatedly commit atrocities with impunity". Parts of north-eastern Nigeria have been affected by years of violence involving jihadist groups and armed gangs, which raid communities, abduct residents and demand ransoms. Similar armed groups operate in the country's north-west and central regions. The latest attack comes as Nigeria prepares for elections next year, with insecurity expected to feature prominently in political debates. - The kidnap gangs, jihadists and separatists wreaking havoc in Nigeria Published 28 November 2025 - 'If you started running, they shot you' - inside Nigeria's growing kidnapping crisis Published 27 August - Inside story of a Nigerian ransom negotiator Published 21 March 2024 Survivors who spoke to AFP said they had counted at least 20 dead. "People were running in different directions to escape the attack," Binnari resident Isiyaku Musa said. "Nobody knew where it was safe to go." Another survivor, Sa'idu Nuhu, said that some people were still missing. Amnesty's Nigeria director, Isa Sanusi, told BBC News on Saturday that the NGO had spoken to some of the bereaved families who said up to 50 people had died. "The initial funeral had 37 people," he said. Sanusi called for an impartial investigation into the killings, accusing the authorities of leaving rural communities "at the mercy of gunmen that are repeatedly commit atrocities with impunity". news.full_article_text: Collegium decisions unanimous, says ex-CJI Chandrachud Former CJI Chandrachud says collegium decisions were unanimous and Kaul endorsed all recommendations, disputing memoir claims of government deference. Former Chief Justice of India (CJI) Dhananjaya Y Chandrachud has responded to former Supreme Court judge Sanjay Kishan Kaul’s account of their interactions over judicial appointments, saying collegium decisions were unanimous and Justice Kaul had endorsed every recommendation. Justice Chandrachud said it would be difficult for him to comment in detail on Kaul’s account in his forthcoming memoir, “Without Fear or Favour”, as he had not yet read the book. “Unless I read his observations and understand the context in which they were made, I would not be in a position to offer a detailed response,” he said. Justice Chandrachud, however, added that the collegium’s official records showed that its resolutions, along with the reasons for its recommendations, were made public on the Supreme Court’s website and that the decisions were unanimous, with Justice Kaul endorsing every recommendation. The former CJI further said there was not a single instance of Justice Kaul recording a dissent when the collegium formally proposed candidates to the government for appointment as judges. He said this was an important part of the record to consider while assessing the decision-making process. He also emphasised that collegium decisions were not arrived at abruptly during meetings. “Judges held multiple rounds of informal and formal discussions before names were officially considered and recommendations sent to the government,” he said, adding that Justice Kaul had never walked out of any such meeting. According to Justice Chandrachud, the meetings were conducted in a congenial atmosphere. Justice Kaul, in his memoir, has said the former CJI was “too deferential to the government”. He has argued that discussions with the executive should not amount to seeking the government’s approval before the collegium has formally deliberated on a candidate. One of his most revealing accounts concerns a candidate from a minority faith whose elevation was questioned by the government. According to Justice Kaul, the government first raised the question of whether the Supreme Court needed additional representation from that faith, despite the candidate being from a state under-represented on the court. A further query concerned the caste to which the candidate’s family had belonged before converting to the faith. The former top court judge found the question irrelevant and the reasoning troubling. He says he told Justice Chandrachud that if appointments were to be made on such considerations, the government might as well appoint judges itself. He then shut the file and walked out of the collegium meeting. The meeting was adjourned, and the government eventually relented. Justice Kaul retired as judge of the Supreme Court in December 2023. He was part of the collegium and authored several important judgments since his elevation to the top court on February 17, 2017. Prior to this, he also served as chief justices of the high courts of Punjab & Haryana and Madras. - Supreme Court Collegium

news.story_lead: At least 2 feared trapped as under-construction building collapses in Delhi's Harsh Vihar An under-construction house collapsed in northeast Delhi’s Harsh Vihar. A Delhi Fire Service (DFS) official said that call regarding the collapse was received at 6.46pm, following which six fire tenders were pressed into service. Police personnel and rescue teams, including the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), rushed to the spot and began efforts to search for anyone who may have been trapped beneath the rubble. However, the circumstances that led to the collapse were not immediately clear, he said. The owner of the structure has been identified and traced, and legal proceedings have been initiated, the police official said, without giving further details. The incident comes amid a string of building collapses that have shined a spotlight on weak enforcement of building safety laws and lack of proper oversight. On October 7, at least four people died when a building collapsed in New Seemapuri with demolition work in an adjacent building, involving vibrating machines, suspected to have triggered the collapse. Unauthorised construction was suspected to be the cause in both the incidents.

news.headline: Serbia Snap Elections See High Turnout Amid Student-Led Opposition Challenge
news.story_lead: Serbia conducted early parliamentary elections featuring a heavy voter turnout of nearly 65% by late afternoon. The snap election follows years of civic unrest driven by a student-led anti-corruption movement challenging the long-standing administration of President Aleksandar Vučić.
news.full_article_text:
### High Turnout Recorded in Serbian Early Elections

Serbia held snap parliamentary elections with preliminary official figures showing a turnout of 64.9% by 18:00 local time (17:00 GMT), two hours prior to the closure of polls across 8,210 voting booths. High turnout levels were observed both domestically and at overseas voting locations in cities like Paris, Munich, Ljubljana, Chicago, and Los Angeles.

### Key Parties and Electoral Dynamics

- **Serbian Progressive Party (SNS)**: Headed by 56-year-old Aleksandar Vučić, who has maintained political dominance since 2012. Having served two presidential terms, Vučić is campaigning to return to the position of Prime Minister. The SNS occupies position number one on the ballot paper.
- **Student List**: Appearing as number three on the ballot, this civic opposition movement is led by Novi Sad University professor Ilija Srdanović. Its list of 250 parliamentary candidates includes educators, medical professionals, actors, and athletes chosen by university assemblies rather than conventional politicians.
- **Protest Origins**: Public demonstrations intensified following a 2024 canopy collapse at a railway station in Novi Sad, which caused 16 fatalities and became a symbol of administrative corruption and infrastructure neglect.

### Electoral Infrastructure and Monitoring Allegations

With 6.45 million registered voters out of a total population of 6.53 million, observers highlighted potential register inaccuracies. Serbian citizens residing in Kosovo and dual citizens in Bosnia also retained voting rights. To prevent potential electoral manipulation, the Student List deployed at least two monitors to every voting station.

Independent monitoring organization CRTA noted numerous irregularities and localized violent incidents. Reports emerged from Niš regarding alleged 'chain voting'—a fraudulent practice where ballot papers are pre-marked prior to entering polling booths.
news.background_context: The snap elections follow two years of student-led anti-corruption protests triggered by the November 2024 train station roof collapse in Novi Sad, which killed 16 people. The tragedy fueled widespread public discontent over official negligence and regulatory oversights.

hindi_translation.story_lead: सर्बिया में मध्यावधि संसदीय चुनाव आयोजित किए गए, जिसमें देर शाम तक लगभग 65% मतदान दर्ज किया गया। यह मध्यावधि चुनाव राष्ट्रपति अलेक्जेंडर वुचिच के लंबे शासन को चुनौती देने वाले छात्र-नेतृत्व वाले भ्रष्टाचार विरोधी आंदोलन के बाद हुआ है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### सर्बियाई मध्यावधि चुनावों में भारी मतदान

सर्बिया में मध्यावधि संसदीय चुनाव आयोजित हुए, जिसमें प्रारंभिक आधिकारिक आंकड़ों के अनुसार 8,210 मतदान केंद्रों पर स्थानीय समयानुसार 18:00 बजे तक 64.9% मतदान हुआ। पेरिस, म्यूनिख, ल्युब्लियाना, शिकागो और लॉस एंजिल्स जैसे शहरों में घरेलू और विदेशी दोनों स्तरों पर उच्च भागीदारी देखी गई।

### प्रमुख दल और चुनावी गतिशीलता

- **सर्बियाई प्रोग्रेसिव पार्टी (SNS)**: 56 वर्षीय अलेक्जेंडर वुचिच के नेतृत्व वाली पार्टी, जो 2012 से सत्ता में है। दो राष्ट्रपति कार्यकाल पूरा करने के बाद, वुचिच प्रधानमंत्री पद पर लौटने के लिए चुनाव लड़ रहे हैं। मतपत्र पर SNS पहले स्थान पर है।
- **स्टूडेंट लिस्ट**: मतपत्र पर तीसरे स्थान पर मौजूद इस नागरिक विपक्षी आंदोलन का नेतृत्व नोवी साद विश्वविद्यालय के प्रोफेसर इलिजा सरडानोविच कर रहे हैं। इनके 250 उम्मीदवारों की सूची में पारंपरिक राजनेताओं के बजाय संकाय सभाओं द्वारा चुने गए शिक्षक, डॉक्टर, अभिनेता और खिलाड़ी शामिल हैं।
- **विरोध का कारण**: नोवी साद में एक रेलवे स्टेशन की छत गिरने से 16 लोगों की मौत के बाद जनता का गुस्सा भड़क उठा, जो प्रशासनिक भ्रष्टाचार और लापरवाही का प्रतीक बन गया।

### चुनावी ढांचा और निगरानी के आरोप

6.53 मिलियन की कुल जनसंख्या में से 6.45 मिलियन पंजीकृत मतदाता होने के कारण, पर्यवेक्षकों ने मतदाता सूची की विश्वसनीयता पर चिंता व्यक्त की। छात्र सूची ने चुनावी धांधली रोकने के लिए प्रत्येक मतदान केंद्र पर कम से कम दो पर्यवेक्षक तैनात किए।

स्वतंत्र निगरानी संगठन CRTA ने कई अनियमितताओं और हिंसक घटनाओं की सूचना दी। नीश (Niş) शहर से 'चेन वोटिंग' (पूर्व-चिह्नित मतपत्रों का अवैध उपयोग) के आरोप सामने आए।

यह चुनाव 2024 में नोवी साद बुनियादी ढांचा हादसे के बाद शुरू हुए दो साल के छात्र विरोध प्रदर्शनों के बाद हुआ है।
